name: Cauliflower-Chickpea Couscous Bowl with Olives, Dried Apricots & Honey-Tahini (Two Ways)

instructions.primary_message: This recipe was created to feed two adults and two young children. You know your child (their tastes and appetite) best. Use this recipe as a template, adjusting ingredients, cooking methods, and portions as needed.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 medium head cauliflower
½ lemon
½ small bunch Italian (flat-leaf) parsley

instructions.primary_message: Separate cauliflower into bite-sized florets and cut stems into smaller pieces. Transfer to a large baking sheet pan.

Drain and rinse chickpeas. Place on paper towels and pat dry, then add to the baking sheet with the cauliflower. Drizzle with oil, season with spices, then stir to combine. Spread out in an even layer.
instructions.secondary_message:
2 (254 g) can garbanzo beans (chickpeas)
extra virgin olive oil
1 tsp smoked paprika
1 tsp garlic powder
1 tsp salt
¼ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast, stirring halfway through, until cauliflower is golden and fork-tender, about 25 minutes. Remove from oven.

While the cauliflower and chickpeas are baking, in a medium saucepan, bring water and salt to a boil over high heat. Once boiling, remove from heat, add couscous, and stir to combine. Cover and let stand for 10 minutes; fluff with a fork right before serving.
instructions.secondary_message:
2 cups water
½ tsp salt
1 cup whole wheat couscous

instructions.primary_message: Meanwhile, preheat a large skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, trim, seed, and medium dice bell peppers.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add bell pepper, salt, and pepper; cook, stirring occasionally until softened, 2-3 minutes. Transfer a ½-cup to a plate and set aside.
instructions.secondary_message:
2 tsp extra virgin olive oil
¼ tsp salt
⅛ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Add broth, tomato paste, and spices to the skillet with the remaining bell pepper, then stir to combine. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat to medium-low and continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until the sauce has thickened, 5-6 minutes.
instructions.secondary_message:
2 cups chicken or vegetable broth
3 tbsp tomato paste
½ tsp cumin, ground
¼ tsp coriander, ground
¼ tsp crushed red pepper
⅛ tsp cinnamon, ground
⅛ tsp salt

instructions.primary_message: Meanwhile, juice lemon into a small bowl. Add tahini, honey, and cayenne pepper, then whisk to combine the tahini sauce. (Add water, a few teaspoons at a time, if needed, to reach a drizzling consistency.) Set aside.
instructions.secondary_message:
2 tbsp tahini
1 tbsp honey
1 pinch cayenne pepper

instructions.primary_message: Cut apricots into bite-sized pieces, then add half to the plate with the cooked bell pepper. Add remaining apricots to the skillet, along with olives, and stir to combine. Remove from heat.

When the cauliflower and chickpeas are done, add 1 ½ cups to the plate. Add remaining cauliflower and chickpeas to the skillet and stir to combine. (Add additional water, if necessary, to reach your desired consistency.) Remove from heat.
Shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves.

FOR THE KID PLATES: Divide 1 cup of couscous between plates, along with reserved cauliflower, chickpeas, bell pepper, and apricots. 

FOR THE ADULT PLATES: Divide remaining couscous, veggies, chickpeas, and sauce between plates or bowls. Drizzle with tahini sauce, sprinkle with parsley, and enjoy!
